evidence.quote: Nicholas Steno, 1669, gets credit for first writing down basic geological principles as laws.
In 1788, James Hutton proposed what would become the foundational principle of geology — uniformitarianism.
In 1815, Smith developed the law of faunal succession
The first geologic time scale was published in 1841 — Powell certainly would have known of it and used it in his geologic trips to the West.
who, in 1862, had calculated an age of the Earth based on thermodynamic modeling
In 1869, the same year Powell launched his expedition, English scientist Thomas Huxley challenged Lord Kelvin’s calculation
It was the discovery of radioactivity in 1896 that changed the heat-flow picture dramatically.
Based on radiometric dating of the oldest rock he could find, English geologist Arthur Holmes in 1913 calculated an age of 1.6 billion years
It was 1956 when Clair Cameron Patterson, an American geochemist, used lead-lead dating

objectives: Order major developments in understanding geologic time from 1669 to 1956 on a timeline
Explain how stratigraphy, uniformitarianism, and faunal succession established relative time before absolute dating
Describe how discovery of radioactivity and lead-lead dating revised the estimated age of Earth
